body:
### Problem

`vim.system(cmd, { timeout = N })` arms its timeout timer right after the spawn without refreshing libuv's cached loop time (`runtime/lua/vim/_system.lua`, the timer started right after `uv.spawn`). libuv measures timer deadlines from the cached loop clock, so if Lua code ran synchronously for longer than N ms before the call, the timer is already overdue when it is started: the child is killed within a millisecond or two and `wait()` returns `code = 124`, `signal = 15`.

`vim.wait()` and a bare `:wait(N)` are not affected (they measured ~528 ms for a 500 ms wait after the same block).

### Steps to reproduce

Save as `repro.lua`, run `nvim --clean --headless -l repro.lua`:

```lua
local uv = vim.uv
local function block(ms) local t = uv.hrtime() while (uv.hrtime() - t) / 1e6 < ms do end end
for _, pre in ipairs({ 0, 1200 }) do
  uv.update_time(); block(pre)
  local t0 = uv.hrtime()
  local r = vim.system({ "sleep", "2" }, { timeout = 500 }):wait()
  print("blocked", pre, "code", r.code, "signal", r.signal, "ms", math.floor((uv.hrtime() - t0) / 1e6))
end
```

### Expected behavior

Both runs are killed by the timeout after ~500 ms (`code 124`, ~500 ms).

### Actual behavior

```
blocked 0     code 124  signal 15  ms 501
blocked 1200  code 124  signal 15  ms 2
```

After the loop was blocked for 1200 ms, the 500 ms timeout fires after ~2 ms. With a command that should finish inside the timeout (`sleep 0.2`), the same effect kills it early and reports `code 124`. Calling `uv.update_time()` immediately before `vim.system` restores the expected behavior.

### Suggested fix

Call `uv.update_time()` (or compute the deadline from `uv.hrtime()`) right before arming the timeout timer in `vim.system`.

### Nvim version

NVIM v0.11.7 (also reproduced on v0.12.5)

### OS

macOS 27 (arm64)
title: vim.system(): timeout fires almost immediately when the event loop was blocked before the spawn
